audit_status.source_base: Greek Hebrews text tradition with Proverbs/Sinai/Zion citation texture; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for cloud of witnesses, endurance, discipline, holiness, Esau, Sinai/Zion contrast, unshakable reign.

verses.restored: Therefore, since we also have so great cloud of witnesses surrounding us, laying aside every weight and the easily entangling sin/misalignment, let us run through endurance the contest set before us,

familiar.text: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

modern.text: Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off every encumbrance and the sin that so easily entangles, and let us run with endurance the race set out for us.

original.text: Τοιγαροῦν καὶ ἡμεῖς, τοσοῦτον ἔχοντες περικείμενον ἡμῖν νέφος μαρτύρων, ὄγκον ἀποθέμενοι πάντα καὶ τὴν εὐπερίστατον ἁμαρτίαν, διʼ ὑπομονῆς τρέχωμεν τὸν προκείμενον ἡμῖν ἀγῶνα,

verses.restored: looking away to Jesus, pioneer/founder and completer of trust, who for joy set before him endured cross, despising shame, and has sat down at right hand of throne of the Divine.

familiar.text: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.

modern.text: Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy set before Him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

original.text: ἀφορῶντες εἰς τὸν τῆς πίστεως ἀρχηγὸν καὶ τελειωτὴν Ἰησοῦν, ὃς ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης αὐτῷ χαρᾶς ὑπέμεινεν σταυρὸν αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας, ἐν δεξιᾷ τε τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ κεκάθικεν.

verses.restored: For consider the one enduring such opposition by sinners/misaligned ones against himself, so that you may not grow weary, fainting in your souls/lives.

familiar.text: For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.

modern.text: Consider Him who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart. God Disciplines His Sons

original.text: Ἀναλογίσασθε γὰρ τὸν τοιαύτην ὑπομεμενηκότα ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν εἰς ⸀ἑαυτοὺς ἀντιλογίαν, ἵνα μὴ κάμητε ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν ἐκλυόμενοι.

verses.restored: You have not yet resisted to blood, struggling against sin/misalignment,

familiar.text: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.

modern.text: In your struggle against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.

original.text: οὔπω μέχρις αἵματος ἀντικατέστητε πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνταγωνιζόμενοι,

verses.restored: and you have forgotten the encouragement that speaks to you as children: My child, do not regard lightly discipline of Lord, nor faint when corrected by him.

familiar.text: And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:

modern.text: And you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord, and do not lose heart when He rebukes you.

original.text: καὶ ἐκλέλησθε τῆς παρακλήσεως, ἥτις ὑμῖν ὡς υἱοῖς διαλέγεται, Υἱέ μου, μὴ ὀλιγώρει παιδείας κυρίου, μηδὲ ἐκλύου ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐλεγχόμενος·

verses.restored: For whom Lord loves he disciplines, and he trains every child whom he receives.

familiar.text: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.

modern.text: For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He chastises every son He receives.”

original.text: ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει, μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται.

verses.restored: Endure into discipline; the Divine deals with you as children. For what child is there whom a parent does not discipline?

familiar.text: If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?

modern.text: Endure suffering as discipline; God is treating you as sons. For what son is not disciplined by his father?

original.text: εἰς παιδείαν ὑπομένετε· ὡς υἱοῖς ὑμῖν προσφέρεται ὁ θεός· τίς ⸀γὰρ υἱὸς ὃν οὐ παιδεύει πατήρ;

verses.restored: But if you are without discipline, of which all have become partners, then you are illegitimate and not children.

familiar.text: But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.

modern.text: If you do not experience discipline like everyone else, then you are illegitimate children and not true sons.

original.text: εἰ δὲ χωρίς ἐστε παιδείας ἧς μέτοχοι γεγόνασι πάντες, ἄρα νόθοι ⸂καὶ οὐχ υἱοί ἐστε⸃.

verses.restored: Furthermore we had fathers of our flesh as discipliners and we respected them; shall we not much more be arranged under Father of spirits and live?

familiar.text: Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?

modern.text: Furthermore, we have all had earthly fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Should we not much more submit to the Father of our spirits and live?

original.text: εἶτα τοὺς μὲν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν πατέρας εἴχομεν παιδευτὰς καὶ ἐνετρεπόμεθα· οὐ ⸀πολὺ μᾶλλον ὑποταγησόμεθα τῷ πατρὶ τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ ζήσομεν;

verses.restored: For they indeed for a few days disciplined according to what seemed good to them, but he for benefit, into sharing his holiness.

familiar.text: For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.

modern.text: Our fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our good, so that we may share in His holiness.

original.text: οἱ μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ὀλίγας ἡμέρας κατὰ τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς ἐπαίδευον, ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ συμφέρον εἰς τὸ μεταλαβεῖν τῆς ἁγιότητος αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Now all discipline for the present does not seem joy but grief, yet afterward it yields peaceful fruit of righteousness/justice to those trained by it.

familiar.text: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.

modern.text: No discipline seems enjoyable at the time, but painful. Later on, however, it yields a harvest of righteousness and peace to those who have been trained by it.

original.text: πᾶσα ⸀δὲ παιδεία πρὸς μὲν τὸ παρὸν οὐ δοκεῖ χαρᾶς εἶναι ἀλλὰ λύπης, ὕστερον δὲ καρπὸν εἰρηνικὸν τοῖς διʼ αὐτῆς γεγυμνασμένοις ἀποδίδωσιν δικαιοσύνης.

verses.restored: Therefore straighten the drooping hands and weakened knees,

familiar.text: Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;

modern.text: Therefore strengthen your limp hands and weak knees.

original.text: Διὸ τὰς παρειμένας χεῖρας καὶ τὰ παραλελυμένα γόνατα ἀνορθώσατε,

verses.restored: and make straight tracks for your feet, so that what is lame may not be dislocated but rather healed.

familiar.text: And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.

modern.text: Make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame may not be disabled, but rather healed. A Call to Holiness (1 Peter 1:13–21)

original.text: καὶ τροχιὰς ὀρθὰς ⸀ποιεῖτε τοῖς ποσὶν ὑμῶν, ἵνα μὴ τὸ χωλὸν ἐκτραπῇ, ἰαθῇ δὲ μᾶλλον.

verses.restored: Pursue peace with all and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord,

familiar.text: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:

modern.text: Pursue peace with everyone, as well as holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.

original.text: Εἰρήνην διώκετε μετὰ πάντων, καὶ τὸν ἁγιασμόν, οὗ χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν κύριον,

verses.restored: watching lest anyone fall short from grace of the Divine; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you and through it many be defiled;

familiar.text: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled;

modern.text: See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God, and that no root of bitterness springs up to cause trouble and defile many.

original.text: ἐπισκοποῦντες μή τις ὑστερῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ, μή τις ῥίζα πικρίας ἄνω φύουσα ἐνοχλῇ καὶ ⸂διʼ αὐτῆς⸃ μιανθῶσιν ⸀πολλοί,

verses.restored: lest there be any sexually immoral/misusing or profane one like Esau, who for one meal sold his birthright.

familiar.text: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.

modern.text: See to it that no one is sexually immoral, or is godless like Esau, who for a single meal sold his birthright.

original.text: μή τις πόρνος ἢ βέβηλος ὡς Ἠσαῦ, ὃς ἀντὶ βρώσεως μιᾶς ἀπέδετο τὰ πρωτοτόκια ⸀ἑαυτοῦ.

verses.restored: For you know that afterward, wishing to inherit blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for change of mind, though seeking it with tears.

familiar.text: For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.

modern.text: For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. He could find no ground for repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears. An Unshakable Kingdom (Exodus 20:18–21; Deuteronomy 5:22–33)

original.text: ἴστε γὰρ ὅτι καὶ μετέπειτα θέλων κληρονομῆσαι τὴν εὐλογίαν ἀπεδοκιμάσθη, μετανοίας γὰρ τόπον οὐχ εὗρεν, καίπερ μετὰ δακρύων ἐκζητήσας αὐτήν.

verses.restored: For you have not come to what is touched and burning fire, and darkness and gloom and storm,

familiar.text: For ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,

modern.text: For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire; to darkness, gloom, and storm;

original.text: Οὐ γὰρ προσεληλύθατε ⸀ψηλαφωμένῳ καὶ κεκαυμένῳ πυρὶ καὶ γνόφῳ καὶ ⸀ζόφῳ καὶ θυέλλῃ

verses.restored: and trumpet sound and voice of words, which those hearing begged that no further word be added to them.

familiar.text: And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which voice they that heard intreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more:

modern.text: to a trumpet blast or to a voice that made its hearers beg that no further word be spoken.

original.text: καὶ σάλπιγγος ἤχῳ καὶ φωνῇ ῥημάτων, ἧς οἱ ἀκούσαντες παρῃτήσαντο ⸀μὴ προστεθῆναι αὐτοῖς λόγον·

verses.restored: For they could not bear what was commanded: Even if a beast touches the mountain, it shall be stoned.

familiar.text: (For they could not endure that which was commanded, And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart:

modern.text: For they could not bear what was commanded: “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”

original.text: οὐκ ἔφερον γὰρ τὸ διαστελλόμενον· Κἂν θηρίον θίγῃ τοῦ ὄρους, λιθοβοληθήσεται·

verses.restored: And so fearful was the appearance that Moses said: I am terrified and trembling.

familiar.text: And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake:)

modern.text: The sight was so terrifying that even Moses said, “I am trembling with fear.”

original.text: καί, οὕτω φοβερὸν ἦν τὸ φανταζόμενον, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν· Ἔκφοβός εἰμι καὶ ἔντρομος.

verses.restored: But you have come to Mount Zion and city of living Divine, heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of messengers in festival gathering,

familiar.text: But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels,

modern.text: Instead, you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have come to myriads of angels

original.text: ἀλλὰ προσεληλύθατε Σιὼν ὄρει καὶ πόλει θεοῦ ζῶντος, Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ, καὶ μυριάσιν ἀγγέλων, πανηγύρει

verses.restored: and to assembly of firstborn ones enrolled in heavens, and to Divine judge of all, and to spirits of righteous/just ones completed,

familiar.text: To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,

modern.text: in joyful assembly, to the congregation of the firstborn, enrolled in heaven. You have come to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,

original.text: καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων ⸂ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς⸃, καὶ κριτῇ θεῷ πάντων, καὶ πνεύμασι δικαίων τετελειωμένων,

verses.restored: and to Jesus mediator of new covenant, and to sprinkled blood/life speaking better than Abel.

familiar.text: And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.

modern.text: to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.

original.text: καὶ διαθήκης νέας μεσίτῃ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ αἵματι ῥαντισμοῦ κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι παρὰ τὸν Ἅβελ.

verses.restored: Watch that you do not refuse the One speaking. For if they did not escape refusing the one warning upon earth, much more we who turn away from the One from heavens,

familiar.text: See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven:

modern.text: See to it that you do not refuse Him who speaks. For if the people did not escape when they refused Him who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we reject Him who warns us from heaven?

original.text: Βλέπετε μὴ παραιτήσησθε τὸν λαλοῦντα· εἰ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι οὐκ ⸀ἐξέφυγον ⸂ἐπὶ γῆς παραιτησάμενοι τὸν⸃ χρηματίζοντα, ⸀πολὺ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς οἱ τὸν ἀπʼ οὐρανῶν ἀποστρεφόμενοι·

verses.restored: whose voice shook the earth then; but now he has promised, saying: Yet once more I shake not only earth but also heaven.

familiar.text: Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.

modern.text: At that time His voice shook the earth, but now He has promised, “Once more I will shake not only the earth, but heaven as well.”

original.text: οὗ ἡ φωνὴ τὴν γῆν ἐσάλευσεν τότε, νῦν δὲ ἐπήγγελται λέγων· Ἔτι ἅπαξ ἐγὼ ⸀σείσω οὐ μόνον τὴν γῆν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν οὐρανόν.

verses.restored: And this, Yet once more, makes clear the removal of things being shaken, as things made, so that the things not shaken may remain.

familiar.text: And this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.

modern.text: The words “Once more” signify the removal of what can be shaken—that is, created things—so that the unshakable may remain.

original.text: τὸ δὲ Ἔτι ἅπαξ δηλοῖ ⸂τῶν σαλευομένων⸃ μετάθεσιν ὡς πεποιημένων, ἵνα μείνῃ τὰ μὴ σαλευόμενα.

verses.restored: Therefore, receiving an unshakable reign, let us have grace, through which we may serve the Divine acceptably with reverence and awe,

familiar.text: Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear:

modern.text: Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us be filled with gratitude, and so worship God acceptably with reverence and awe.

original.text: διὸ βασιλείαν ἀσάλευτον παραλαμβάνοντες ἔχωμεν χάριν, διʼ ἧς ⸀λατρεύωμεν εὐαρέστως τῷ θεῷ μετὰ ⸂εὐλαβείας καὶ δέους⸃,

verses.restored: for our Divine is consuming fire.

familiar.text: For our God is a consuming fire.

modern.text: “For our God is a consuming fire.”

original.text: καὶ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον.

translation_notes: Discipline language must be handled carefully; it is training toward healing and justice-fruit, not sanctification of abuse.
Sinai/Zion contrast should not be anti-Jewish; both are Israel's sacred imagery, with Hebrews emphasizing access and unshakable reign.
Healing of the lame and pursuit of peace are central pastoral aims.
safety_note: Do not use Hebrews 12 discipline language to justify abusive parenting, spiritual coercion, or suffering as inherently good. The text points toward healing, peaceful fruit of justice, grace, and unshakable life.
